evidence_references: Apollo PR #292 merged the protected Airspy policy correction; PR #295 allocated Apollo 2.3.4 Build 217 from origin/main b0abf0720bd3c80143fc6145e4b96d592804197e. The required release-security-contract check passed on the reviewed allocation head. Build 216 RF corrections remain in source.

Approved aarch64 runner apollo-kd6kpc-14 built one receiver-neutral ZIP with RTL-SDR, Airspy R2, SDRplay RSP1B readiness, and KA9Q radiod. Two builds at the same canonical source path and timestamp were byte-identical: SHA-256 e9ac2ec207fc6a1398641c43ba1de1415f5ad791efe86857a169d6185e713a0f, 18,574,147 bytes.

Final ZIP extraction verified 121 packaged files, package inventory SHA-256 bbcbf83236027f9b62cf7e86db69e74386ef21e1b843cef30069dc69fc311753, 50 protected-controller entries, protected manifest SHA-256 dce7e31dc8c5505aba5aa8165d81c0ce8b7ede2cb5462c19e9e080caa6bfc23a, and the packaged Airspy policy against its packaged controller.

Native ARM64 package tests: 129 passed, 3 skipped; receiver tests: 81 passed; broader controller tests: 284 passed, 2 skipped; selected recovery tests: 24 passed, 5 skipped. All groups had zero failures. ARM64 ELF and principal dynamic-dependency checks passed. No production node was contacted during qualification.
